stories.title: Yemen’s Houthis report attack on Saudi oil tanker in Red Sea
stories.summary: Saudi shipping company Bahri confirmed its vessel was struck, all crew members safe. The Houthis rebel group have claimed an attack on a Saudi oil tanker off the port city of Yanbu in the Red Sea. The Yemeni group issued a statement on Monday detailing its strike on the “Amzan,” the latest targeting of Saudi assets by the Houthis in support of Iran, and heightening fears that the US-Iran war could escalate across the region. A Houthi military spokesperson said that a vessel belonging to Saudi national shipping company Bahri “was targeted off the coast of Yanbu in Saudi Arabia with a ballistic missile”. Bahri later released a statement confirming that the “Amzan”, was involved in a maritime incident in the Red Sea. Bahri said it remained in contact with the vessel and was closely coordinating with the relevant authorities. It added that all crew members were safe and no injuries had been reported. “The safety of our people, the protection of the maritime environment, and the safe management of the vessel remain our highest priorities,” the statement said. There has been no confirmation from Saudi officials. An Al Jazeera request for comment to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs received no response. In recent weeks, the Houthis killed seven people in a Yemeni port and targeted an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. They also killed at least six people and wounded 10 others in a double-tap strike on a cargo vessel in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

stories.title: Violence flares in Haiti as gang attack kills 30 people
stories.summary: Island nation grapples with violence as it seeks to hold first elections in more than a decade. At least 30 people have been killed as a new wave of violence grips Haiti. A powerful gang coalition mounted the deadly attack on a farming community in Kenscoff, south of the capital, Port-au-Prince, late on Sunday, officials reported. The flare-up in violence comes as Haiti hopes to hold its first general election in more than a decade. Jean Massillon, Kenscoff’s mayor, said armed men “sowed chaos” as they set homes on fire and killed residents. He said gang members targeted a church and homes, including that of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert. Massillon blamed the attack on members of Viv Ansanm, a group that was designated as a “foreign terrorist organisation” by the United States government last year. Gangs control an estimated 70 percent of Port-au-Prince. Viv Ansanm has repeatedly targeted Kenscoff, which occupies a strategic position overlooking routes into Petion-Ville, where several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government are located. A United Nations-backed gang suppression force is mandated to help police fight the gangs and restore order, but it has not yet reached its full capacity of 5,500 members. According to the UN, gang violence has displaced 1.5 million people across Haiti. The violence has persisted despite efforts to rein it in.
